title: Scientists Make Cookies from Plastic Waste
paragraphs: An old plastic bottle probably isn't the first thing you think of when you're hungry. But that may change, as scientists in America have found a way to make cookies from old plastic!
Researchers at Southern Illinois University Carbondale have developed a way to turn plastic into proteins, fats and flavorings using genetically modified yeast.

Lahiru Jayakody, who led the project, told The Guardian that his team got the idea because both plastic and food contain carbon. So they wanted to see if carbon from plastic could be used to make food.

The researchers used PET — one of the most common types of plastic, often used to make single-use water bottles. They found a way to break this plastic down using water and oxygen at high temperatures and pressures, creating smaller molecules containing carbon.

These molecules are then fed to genetically modified yeast, which turns the carbon into proteins, fats and other nutrients. The mixture is finally combined with starch and passed through a 3D printer to create a disc-shaped cookie.

So, what do these cookies taste like? Well, nobody knows, as the researchers are still waiting for approval to test them on humans. However, they say people have reacted positively to the cookies' smell!
And cookies are just one possibility, as the proteins produced by the yeast could also be turned into other kinds of food.

The technology was developed for NASA's Deep Space Food Challenge, which looked for new ways to feed astronauts on long space journeys. A round trip to Mars, for example, could take three years, so astronauts would need to make careful use of everything they have.

But the idea could be useful on Earth too. The team says the technology could be used on long submarine journeys, in disaster areas, or even help deal with plastic waste pollution and people's everyday food needs.
Before that happens, however, there may be another challenge — convincing people to eat food produced this way. After all, a cookie made from an old plastic bottle could take some getting used to!
